I farm here in Mtwara on my own land, about one hectare and a bit for sorghum this season, and I mix in some cowpea between the rows like my father did. I have no money for the shop fertilizer — one bag costs too much and nobody around here puts that on sorghum anyway, we save any small cash for cashew. I keep my own seed from last harvest, the sorghum we always plant, it knows this sandy soil and the dry spells. The rain here comes when it comes, I cannot water the field, so I work with my wife and the older children and we weed two times with the hoe.
